blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Legal-content reproduction requires matching the source exactly in section hierarchy, verbatim text, citations, and amendment spans; a dropped citation or mislabeled amendment carries into the products lawyers rely on. We report an industrial pipeline converting U.S. state legislation into strict, schema-constrained XML, and hypothesize that its accuracy comes from harness engineering, the deterministic tooling built around a model, more than the model itself. Our controlled ablation crosses three harnesses (zero-shot, a single tool-using agent, and a decomposed multi-agent pipeline) with three Claude models on 153 gold bills from two jurisdictions. The harness narrows the model gap: the weakest model in the full pipeline beats the strongest model alone (0.948 versus 0.806, paired bootstrap p less than 0.001). Because the two agentic harnesses share identical tools, their gap comes from orchestration: decomposition plus the persisted state and per-agent context it brings. Across four scored dimensions, the model spread at zero-shot (0.68 to 0.81) narrows to 0.95 at the full pipeline; the residual sits almost entirely in citation normalization, where the canonical identifier is retrieved from an external authority rather than generated from the weights, so a deterministic lookup tool supplies the exactness that a larger model does not.
blocks.zh: 法律内容的复制要求将来源精确地按照节级、逐字记录、引文和修正的跨度加以匹配;律师所依赖的产品中附带的引文或标签错误的修正。 我们报告一条工业管道 将美国州立法转换成严格的, 受计划约束的XML, 并假设它的准确性来自 利用工程, 决定性的工具 围绕一个模型, 超过模型本身。 我们的受控喷发横跨了三条绳索(零射线,一个单一的工具使用剂,以及一个分解的多剂管道),在两个管辖区153个金币上有三个克劳德模型. 牵引装置缩小了模型间隙:整个输油管中最弱的模型仅比最强的模型(0.948对0.806,配对的靴子圈p小于0.001). 由于两支代理吊带共用相同的工具,它们的空白来自于管弦:分解加它带来的持续状态和每代理上下文. 在四个得分的维度上,模型以零射法(0.68至0.81)在全管上传播到0.95;剩余部分几乎完全坐落在引号正常化中,从外部权威处获取犬科识别剂而不是从权重中生成,所以一个定型的望镜工具提供了更大的模型所没有的准确性.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Most legal-NLP benchmarks reward understanding. Classification, retrieval, judgment
prediction, and summarization all ask whether a system recovers the meaning or the right
label, and a paraphrase that keeps the substance usually counts as correct. Reproduction
is a different problem. Once a bill becomes a product that lawyers rely on, the output has to
match the source down to the surface: sections and subsections in the right order, the bill
text verbatim, citations in canonical form, the struck and inserted spans of an amendment
placed where they belong, and the metadata that indexes it downstream. A dropped citation or a
mislabeled amendment is an error that travels into the products lawyers put in front of clients,
wherever in the document it happens to sit. What we are after is exact reproduction, not a high
average.

blocks.en:
A large enough model might be expected to clear this bar on its own. It does not. In the
zero-shot condition (T1), even the strongest model we tested falls short: Opus reaches only 0.806 0.806 overall and barely resolves jurisdiction-specific citations (normalization 0.232 0.232 ).
The shortfall is not obviously something a larger model fixes. A model has no way to know a jurisdiction’s
normalized statutory identifiers from pre-training, since that mapping lives in an external
authority rather than in the weights, and making the model larger does little to close the gap.

blocks.en:
Our working hypothesis is that exactness here owes more to harness engineering, the
orchestration, tools, and deterministic constraints assembled around the model, than to the model
itself. To test it we cross three harnesses with three models (§ 4 ): T1 runs the
model zero-shot with no harness, T2 hands a single agent the full tool set and asks it to
self-sequence the conversion, and T3 is the decomposed harness modeled on the production system,
splitting that same tool set across specialized agents. Because T2 and T3 share tools exactly,
whatever separates them should reflect orchestration—decomposition together with the persisted
state and per-agent context it brings—not a wider action space.

blocks.en:
We make four contributions. (1) A deployed harness : a playbook-driven, multi-agent
pipeline that converts U.S. state legislation into schema-constrained publication XML and runs
in production at a legal-content publisher (§ 4 ). (2) A controlled
model × \times harness ablation that holds tool access constant between the single-agent (T2) and
decomposed (T3) harnesses, which lets us attribute the gain to orchestration—decomposition, the persisted
state it introduces, and per-agent context isolation—rather than to a larger action space (§ 6 ). (3) A dimension-resolved error analysis showing the residual error is not spread evenly
but settles in the legally load-bearing dimensions, citations and amendments, and on the harder
jurisdiction (§ 6 ). Handing the citation-lookup tool to a single agent at T2 does
not appear to be enough on its own: only the stronger models invoke it well (normalization 0.88 0.88 and 0.59 0.59 for Sonnet and Opus against Haiku’s 0.10 0.10 ), and the weakest recovers only once T3

citation score split into localization and normalization. That split is what localizes the
residual to citation normalization, which no model in our study resolves unaided (§ 5 ).

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Systems that convert raw documents into structured markup, such as the OCR-free parsers
Nougat ( Blecher et al., 2024 ) and GOT-OCR ( Wei et al., 2024 ) , are judged with the fidelity
metrics we also use: normalized edit distance ( Levenshtein, 1966 ) and Tree-Edit-Distance
Similarity ( Zhong et al., 2020 ) , codified by OmniDocBench ( Ouyang et al., 2025 ) . A closer
benchmark, ParseBench ( Zhang et al., 2026a ) , finds no method consistently strong across
dimensions, so general-purpose parsing is not yet solved even before any legal requirement enters.
None of this work, though, scores against a schema with legal-semantic markup such as amendment
spans and resolved citations, at our largest documents’ scale (§ 3 ), or as a function
of system architecture. Our schema also differs from the legislative-markup standards
USLM 1 1 1 https://github.com/usgpo/uslm and Akoma
Ntoso 2 2 2 https://www.oasis-open.org/committees/tc_home.php?wg_abbrev=legaldocml (the
OASIS LegalDocML standard), since we evaluate against a fixed, confidential in-house schema.
Grammar-constrained decoding ( Geng et al., 2023 ) is related but separate: it guarantees
well-formed output at inference time, which is not the same as measuring a full pipeline’s fidelity
once assembled.

blocks.en:
Our T3 pipeline draws on now-standard agentic patterns: reasoning interleaved with tool
calls ( Yao et al., 2023 ; Schick et al., 2023 ) and role-specialized
agents ( Wu et al., 2024 ; Hong et al., 2024 ) . Benchmarks for such
systems ( Liu et al., 2024 ; Jimenez et al., 2024 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ) tend to score task
completion and usually vary tool access and decomposition together, so a gain from adding agents is
hard to separate from adding tools. A more recent line names the surrounding infrastructure the harness and argues it, not the base model, often decides whether a capability becomes a
finished task. Harness-Bench ( Yao et al., 2026 ) reports capability at the
model × \times harness level, while Zhang et al. (2026b) argue comparisons stay uninterpretable
unless the harness is disclosed and held fixed. We add a domain instance under conditions that line
has not jointly imposed. We grade against a hard exactness bar rather than completion, so the claim
that the harness matters is tested where being almost right already counts as failure. And our
T2-versus-T3 contrast is the fixed-harness comparison Zhang et al. (2026b) ask for, tools held
identical while decomposition varies, which lets the gain read as orchestration rather than a
larger action space.

blocks.en:
Applied legal NLP tends to grade a coarser correctness. Benchmarks like
LegalBench ( Guha et al., 2023 ) and CUAD ( Hendrycks et al., 2021 ) score classification,
extraction, and QA on label accuracy or span F 1 F_{1} , tolerating a near-miss that a legal-publishing

law. Work on statutory citation processing ( Darji et al., 2026 ) has treated resolution as a
standalone extraction task. We measure it instead as one dimension of a full pipeline, split into
localization and normalization (§ 5 ). Exact reproduction of a structured legal
document remains comparatively understudied relative to the effort it absorbs.

blocks.en: 3 Task and Dataset
blocks.zh: 3 任务和数据集

blocks.en:
The task is to convert a legislative bill PDF into structured XML that reproduces the bill
exactly, down to its section hierarchy, verbatim text, statutory citations, and amendment spans, and that validates against a fixed publication schema.
blocks.zh:
任务是将PDF立法法案转换为结构化的XML,以复制法案
确切地说, 依次到它的章节顺序, 逐字记录, 法定引用, 和修正的跨度, 并验证一个固定的出版物计划。

blocks.en: Our inputs are the legislative PDFs that state legislatures publish, here from the Idaho Legislature 3 3 3 https://legislature.idaho.gov/sessioninfo/ and the New Jersey Legislature. 4 4 4 https://www.njleg.state.nj.us/bill-search They bring all the difficulty of real legal typography: running headers and footers, margins, multi-column layouts, and footnotes. Amendatory bills add inline formatting on top of this, underline for inserted material and strikethrough for deleted material, which has to be recovered exactly rather than approximately. Text frequently spills across page and column boundaries, so getting the reading order right means reassembling content across physical breaks. Appendix A works a real public Idaho bill through the full PDF → \rightarrow XML pipeline as an example.

blocks.en: The output has to validate against a strict publication XML schema constrained by a DTD (Document Type Definition), which we keep confidential. It encodes the section hierarchy (title, chapter, section, subsection, with typed paragraph containers), the verbatim bill text, citations resolved to existing statutory identifiers, amendment markup as typed inline elements for added and deleted material, and metadata for indexing. Validity is all-or-nothing, since a single misplaced element can invalidate the whole document. Appendix A shows this amendment markup worked through on a real bill.

By harness we mean the deterministic engineering built around the model: typed tools, schema
validation, per-jurisdiction configuration, and structural boundaries that fix what the model
produces at each step. The three harnesses add this scaffolding in increasing amounts, none in
T1, tools in T2, tools plus decomposition in T3 (Figure 1 ), and the paper’s
question is how much exactness each layer contributes.

its canonical identifier, a limitation that dominates the results.

blocks.en:
A single aggregate similarity score cannot distinguish “reads almost the same” from “cites
the wrong law,” and for this task that distinction is the entire point. The errors that matter tend to be small ones: a section renumbered, a struck word left standing, a citation resolved to the
wrong statute. Any of them can still change what a bill proposes to do. Because a bill is only a proposed change, such an error does not corrupt the enacted statute. Its cost lands downstream instead, in how the change gets reported, since acting on a misstated bill can be costly even when the error never reaches the session law. Passing schema validation does not certify any of this: it confirms the document is well-formed and structurally complete (§ 3 ), not that its content is right, which is why validity and content correctness have to be scored separately. We therefore break correctness into four independent evaluation dimensions, each scored separately: Textual
Integrity (the body reproduced without omission, hallucination, or mutation); Layout Topology (the section/subsection/paragraph hierarchy reconstructed as the correct XML tree); Legislative Mutations (inline added.material / deleted.material spans
marking exactly which words a bill inserts or strikes); and Citation Fidelity (statutory cross-references localized in the text and resolved to the canonical identifier).

blocks.en: Every cell mean in § 6 carries a 95% confidence interval from a bootstrap over that cell’s scored documents (10,000 resamples, fixed seed). For the comparisons our claims rest on, such as Haiku ⋅ \cdot T3 against Opus ⋅ \cdot T1 or Sonnet against Opus within a tier, we run a paired bootstrap over documents scored in both arms, matched by identity, and report a two-sided p p -value on the mean difference. We prefer this to a chi-squared test, since our scores are continuous on [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] rather than pass/fail counts and binning them would discard information the bootstrap keeps. This captures variance across the document sample , not run-to-run variance, as each cell is a single run. The staircase is clean and monotonic for every model, and the model gap shrinks at every step. Moving Haiku from zero-shot to the full system raises Overall from 0.677 0.677 to 0.948 0.948 , whereas moving from Haiku to Opus at zero-shot raises it only from 0.677 0.677 to 0.806 0.806 : the harness lifts more than the model does. blocks.en: One result complicates the “Haiku < < Sonnet < < Opus” ranking. At T2, Sonnet’s Overall ( 0.922 0.922 ) edges out Opus’s ( 0.910 0.910 ), a gap a paired bootstrap cannot distinguish from noise ( p = 0.39 p=0.39 , n = 151 n=151 ). What is robust is the dimension underneath. The gap is almost entirely in citations, where Sonnet resolves far better than Opus at T2 (localization 0.869 0.869 vs. 0.631 0.631 , normalization 0.881 0.881 vs. 0.593 0.593 , at p = 0.004 p=0.004 and p < 0.001 p<0.001 , n = 74 n=74 ), while structure and text are near-tied, so the composite dilutes a 24-to-29-point (on the 0–1 scale) citation gap below significance. The reversal is specific to T2, so tier alone does not predict which model best exploits a harness. The model axis reads as weak (Haiku) versus strong (Sonnet and Opus, trading the lead) rather than a clean three-point ranking.

blocks.en: Figure 3: Citation normalization is near-zero for every model unaided and is delivered by the harness. The stronger models resolve citations as soon as they have the tool (T2). The weakest model does not, and reaches parity only under full decomposition (T3).

blocks.en: The sharpest split in the model × \times harness interaction shows up here (Figure 3 ). Haiku goes from near-zero (T1 .024 .024 ) to resolving citations only once the harness is fully decomposed (T2 .103 .103 , T3 .801 .801 ), whereas Sonnet and Opus resolve well as soon as they have the lookup tool at all (T2 cite-norm .881 .881 and .593 .593 , up from T1 .282 .282 and .232 .232 ). The same tool gives the strong models a large jump and the weak one almost none until decomposition is added. We read that as the dedicated citation agent substituting for a capability Haiku lacks rather than merely adding one, though the measurement shows only the gap, not its cause. Localization is separable from normalization, not its easier half: at T1 Sonnet localizes worse than Haiku ( .185 .185 vs. .206 .206 ) yet normalizes far better once a citation is found ( .282 .282 vs. .024 .024 ). Since T1 has no lookup tool by construction, its near-zero normalization floor is not the finding. What matters is how unevenly that floor is escaped once the tool arrives, and only for the model that also gets a dedicated agent.
blocks.zh: 模型 ×\times 牵引相互作用中最尖锐的分裂出现在这里(图3). Haiku从近零(T1.024.024)开始,只有在吊带完全分解后(T2.103.103.103.、T3.801.801.801.)才能解决引文问题,而Sonnet和Opus则在获得检索工具后立即解决(T2引文-Norm 881.881和593.593,比T1.282.282和232.232.32高)。 同一种工具使强模型有一个大跳跃,弱者一个几乎没有,直到分解被添加. 我们读到,作为取代海库能力的专用引用剂缺乏而不是仅仅添加一个,尽管测量只显示差距,而不是其原因。 本地化与正常化是分开的,而不是比较容易的一半:在T1 Sonnet,本地化程度比Haiku差(185.185 vs. 206.206),但一旦找到引用(282. 282 vs. 024. 024),本地化程度要好得多。 由于T1没有通过构建来寻找工具,因此其近乎零正常化的地板并不是发现. 重要的是,一旦工具到达,该楼层是如何不均匀地逃过一劫,而且只为同样获得专用代理的模型逃过一劫.

blocks.en: To characterize what is left, we diffed predicted against gold cite.query resolutions for every T3 output with imperfect normalization (32 of 167 outputs containing at least one cite.query node, pooled across the three T3 models, detailed in Appendix Table 7 ). The dominant mode is a dropped subset . Most citations resolve, but a group is silently omitted, typically those in a statutory title the resolution step never reaches (NJ SB 3587). Rarer are granularity errors (ID SB 1023), lookup misses (ID SB 1142), and one over-expansion outlier that alone inflates Idaho’s raw residual (ID SB 1008). The dominant modes look coverage-limited rather than reasoning-limited: they are what we would expect when the codes service returns no identifier, the same per-jurisdiction dependency we flag as a generalization risk (see the Limitations section).

blocks.en: 6.4 Reliability: the tail collapses
blocks.zh: 6.4 可靠性:尾部坍塌

blocks.en: Means understate the case for the harness. What matters is how often it produces a badly wrong document, and any inaccuracy is costly whether or not it is substantive, so the risk to manage is the low-scoring tail, not the average. Table 3 reports the pooled variance and the rate of low-scoring documents ( < 0.70 <0.70 ) by harness. Variance is non-monotonic: T2 is the widest, not the narrowest, before the full pipeline collapses it. At T1 the low-score rate splits sharply by model ( 52 % 52\% Haiku, 23 % 23\% Opus, 19 % 19\% Sonnet), then falls, pooled across models, to 8 % 8\% at T2 and 4 % 4\% at T3. Haiku ⋅ \cdot T2 is the single most unstable cell (std 0.248 0.248 ). That is the measurement; our explanation for it is that a weak model asked to self-sequence is erratic, and that what steadies it is orchestration rather than a stronger model. The per-document distribution behind these statistics appears in Appendix Figure 7 .

blocks.en: Before the final numbers, we sanity-checked every output for integrity and re-ran flagged cases to tell transient errors from stable failures. This caught 7 of 459 T1 attempts ( 1.5 % 1.5\% ) and 21 of 459 T2 attempts ( 4.6 % 4.6\% ), concentrated on the largest New Jersey bills, and repeated runs reproduced them, so we record them as stable properties of the harness rather than transient noise. That T2 fails more often than T1 is the observation; the explanation we offer is that it asks one model to self-sequence extraction, conversion, lookups, and validation in a single context, spending output and context budget on orchestration. The failures run both ways. AB 3678 (302k gold chars) truncates to ≈ \approx 4.7k at T2, while AB 4878 over-generates to ≈ \approx 2.1 × \times gold for all three models identically. T3, sharing the same tool access, avoids both.

More importantly, the thesis holds more strongly on the harder jurisdiction: the gap between Sonnet in the full system and Opus unaided (Sonnet ⋅ \cdot T3 − - Opus ⋅ \cdot T1) is + 0.117 +0.117 on Idaho and + 0.174 +0.174 on New Jersey. blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
We asked whether exactness here is bought with a bigger model or a better harness, and our
experiments lean firmly toward the harness. Scores climb a clean staircase, and the weakest model
in the full pipeline beats the strongest model unaided (Haiku ⋅ \cdot T3 0.948 0.948 against
Opus ⋅ \cdot T1 0.806 0.806 ). Because T2 and T3 keep tools constant, the further climb comes from
orchestration—decomposition, the state persistence it brings, and per-agent context—not from
more tooling. The pipeline also draws
very different models together, tightens the distribution, thins the low-scoring tail, and supplies
the dimension that carries the most legal weight, citation normalization, which no model reaches
unaided. The reason is specific: a citation’s canonical identifier comes from a lookup against an
external authority, not from the weights, so a deterministic tool plus the decomposition that
reliably invokes it delivers what a larger model alone does not (§ 6.3 ).
Every result here comes from a single model family (Claude Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.6
and Opus 4.6); whether the harness effect transfers to other model families is
untested, and we leave it to future work.

task carrying the most legal risk, where being almost right is not good enough. This is where human judgment belongs: expert review is a permanent part
of the architecture, not a temporary crutch. Because the residual is concentrated and identifiable,
it can be routed, with the system auto-publishing what it has solved and surfacing the citation
and amendment decisions that carry legal weight for an editor to confirm. The chief open problem is confidence estimates calibrated well enough to drive that routing. The
same pattern likely holds wherever an exactness bar meets an external source of truth that
pretraining cannot supply, as in medical coding or regulatory tagging: wire that lookup in as a
deterministic tool, decompose so it is reliably invoked, and route the residual to expert review.

blocks.en: Ethical Considerations
blocks.zh: 道德考虑

blocks.en: The system operates where errors can carry legal consequences, so our results are as much a caution as an endorsement of automation. The residual error concentrates in the dimensions that carry legal meaning, citations and amendments, which is exactly where over-trust would do the most harm. Human review of those decisions is therefore not an optional refinement but a requirement for responsible deployment. The evaluation uses expert-produced gold and involves no personal data.
blocks.zh: 该系统在错误可能产生法律后果的地方运作,因此我们的结果与认可自动化一样是谨慎的。 剩余错误集中在具有法律意义、引证和修正的方面,这正是过度信任将造成最大伤害的地方。 因此,对这些决定进行人文审查并不是一种可选的改进,而是负责任地部署的要求。 评估使用专家生产的黄金,不涉及个人数据。

The four dimensions of § 5 —five measures, once citations are split—each score a
different part of the fragment above. Textual integrity compares the running words of the
paragraph, “The commission shall give at least ten (10) days’ written notice …”, against
the gold text character by character, and penalizes a dropped “(10)” or a changed “ten”. Layout topology ignores those words and checks only the shape: a section holding a heading and a para , in that order. Legislative mutations checks the two
inline spans, requiring deleted.material to carry exactly “registered or certified mail”
and added.material exactly “email or certified mail”; swapping the two tags, or dropping
either span, counts as a miss even though every word is still present on the page. Citation fidelity splits in two here: localization asks whether “Section 72-713, Idaho
Code” was found and wrapped in a cite.query at all, and normalization asks whether the
resolved attribute carries the correct statutory identifier—the step no model completed unaided
(§ 6.3 ).

blocks.en: Table 6: Stress-bill collapse and recovery, T1 vs. T3, both scored on Sonnet, the only model with a completed run on these two documents (so the pattern is not verified to generalize to Haiku or Opus). TEDS is unscored under the node cap, but every scorable dimension moves from abandoned to solved.
